uncited: This method implements a Sparse Voxel Octree (SVO) directly on the GPU to support real-time voxel cone tracing and other volume rendering techniques.

It solves the memory inefficiency of dense grids by using linked nodes in linear video memory, organized into 2x2x2 node tiles, while storing actual voxel data in a 3D texture (brick pool) to enable hardware tri-linear interpolation.
Unlike its siblings, it relies on a specific linear memory layout with explicit neighbor buffers and level-start indices rather than implicit spatial indexing or complex pointer chasing.
- `OCTREE_NODE_POOL_NEIGHBOR_N`: Six buffer textures for neighbor information (X, X_NEGATIVE, Y, Y_NEGATIVE, Z, Z_NEGATIVE).
**Octree Pool**: Contains linked nodes organized in 2x2x2 node tiles.
Each node contains 1 pointer to a node-tile (child node).
Sparse voxelization is performed in two steps: 1.
**Voxelize Mesh**: Voxelize the mesh at the target level resolution.
**Tag Octree Nodes**: Process the voxel fragments to tag nodes in the octree.
**Constraint:** Every node has at least one child node unless it is the last level.
The following pseudocode outlines the data structure access and traversal logic based on the source definitions.
Note that specific shader implementations are not provided in the sources, so the traversal is described conceptually.
-   **Boundaries:** Neighbor buffers (`OCTREE_NODE_POOL_NEIGHBOR_N`) must handle boundary conditions where a node has no neighbor in a specific direction.
